questions.text: A 32-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a high-speed road traffic accident. His pulse is 136/min and BP is 76/50 mm Hg despite 1 L of crystalloid and 2 units of O-negative blood. The abdomen is distended and tender. FAST shows free fluid in Morison's pouch and the splenorenal recess. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Serial abdominal examination with repeat FAST in 30 minutes
questions.explanation: A hemodynamically unstable patient with a positive FAST needs immediate laparotomy. CT is reserved for patients who are stable or respond to resuscitation.

questions.text: A 48-year-old man on long-term NSAIDs for osteoarthritis presents with sudden severe epigastric pain that spread over the whole abdomen. On examination the abdomen is board-like and liver dullness is lost. His erect chest X-ray is shown. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: A crescent of free gas under the right hemidiaphragm on an erect film means a hollow viscus has perforated. With NSAID use and sudden epigastric pain, a perforated peptic ulcer is the most likely cause.

questions.text: A 7-year-old girl has many brief staring spells each day. EEG shows generalized 3 Hz spike-and-wave discharges, and she has no other seizure types. What is the drug of choice?
questions.explanation: Ethosuximide is preferred for pure absence seizures. Carbamazepine and phenytoin can make absence seizures worse.

questions.text: Fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus is most likely to injure which nerve?
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve and the posterior circumflex humeral artery wind around the surgical neck. Injury causes deltoid weakness and loss of sensation over the regimental badge area.

questions.text:
Match the tumour markers with the malignancies in which they are most characteristically raised:
Column AColumn B
A. Alpha-fetoprotein1. Medullary carcinoma thyroid
B. CA-1252. Hepatocellular carcinoma
C. CA 19-93. Epithelial ovarian cancer
D. Calcitonin4. Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
questions.explanation: AFP is raised in HCC, CA-125 in epithelial ovarian cancer, CA 19-9 in pancreatic cancer and calcitonin in medullary carcinoma thyroid.

questions.text: Psammoma bodies are characteristically seen in all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Psammoma bodies are laminated calcified concretions found in papillary thyroid carcinoma, serous ovarian tumours, meningioma and mesothelioma. They are not a feature of follicular carcinoma.

questions.text: A 58-year-old diabetic smoker has had crushing retrosternal chest pain for 1 hour. His ECG is shown. Which coronary artery is most likely occluded?
questions.explanation: ST elevation in V1-V4 is an anterior (anteroseptal) wall STEMI, which is usually caused by occlusion of the LAD.

questions.text: Herd immunity does NOT protect susceptible people against which of the following diseases?
questions.explanation: Tetanus comes from spores in the environment and does not spread from person to person. Immunizing others therefore gives no indirect protection.

questions.text: A 22-year-old primigravida at 35 weeks has a generalized tonic-clonic seizure. Her BP is 168/112 mm Hg and urine shows 3+ protein. Which drug is most appropriate to prevent further seizures?
questions.explanation: Magnesium sulphate (Pritchard or Zuspan regimen) is the anticonvulsant of choice in eclampsia. It is better than diazepam and phenytoin at preventing recurrent seizures.

questions.text: A 62-year-old lifelong strict vegetarian has fatigue, tingling in both feet and reduced vibration sense in the lower limbs. Hb is 8.2 g/dL and MCV is 118 fL. His peripheral smear is shown. Which deficiency is most likely?
questions.explanation: A hypersegmented neutrophil (6 lobes) with macro-ovalocytes indicates megaloblastic anaemia. Neurological involvement (subacute combined degeneration) and a vegetarian diet point to B12 rather than folate deficiency.

questions.text: A 6-month-old infant has had low-grade fever, rhinorrhoea, tachypnoea and wheeze for 2 days during the winter months. What is the most common causative organism?
questions.explanation: This is acute bronchiolitis, and RSV is its most common cause, typically in infants under 2 years during winter.

questions.text: A farmer from a hilly district has had high fever, headache and myalgia for 6 days. A painless black eschar is found in the axilla. What is the drug of choice?
questions.explanation: Fever with an eschar suggests scrub typhus (Orientia tsutsugamushi). Doxycycline is the drug of choice, and azithromycin is used in pregnancy and young children.

questions.text: A 55-year-old woman with known gallstones presents with fever with chills, jaundice and right upper quadrant pain. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Fever, jaundice and RUQ pain form Charcot's triad of acute cholangitis. Hypotension and altered sensorium added to these make Reynolds' pentad.

questions.text: A 26-year-old woman has weight loss, heat intolerance, a diffuse goitre, bilateral proptosis and pretibial myxoedema. Which antibody is responsible for her hyperthyroidism?
questions.explanation: In Graves' disease, TSH receptor-stimulating antibodies (TRAb/TSI) drive excess hormone production. Anti-TPO (anti-microsomal) antibodies are markers of thyroid autoimmunity and do not cause it.

questions.text: Cherry-red post-mortem lividity is characteristic of poisoning with:
questions.explanation: Carboxyhaemoglobin gives a cherry-red colour. H2S gives greenish lividity, nitrites give chocolate-brown (methaemoglobin), and phosphorus gives dark brown or yellowish lividity.

questions.text: A 65-year-old hypertensive man suddenly loses vision painlessly in one eye. Fundoscopy shows a pale, oedematous retina with a cherry-red spot at the macula. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: In CRAO the retina becomes ischaemic and opaque, and the thin fovea lets the intact choroidal circulation show through as a cherry-red spot.

questions.text: A patient with treatment-resistant schizophrenia is started on clozapine. Which adverse effect makes regular monitoring of the absolute neutrophil count mandatory?
questions.explanation: Clozapine can cause potentially fatal agranulocytosis, so the ANC must be monitored regularly, most closely in the first 18 weeks.

questions.text: Wickham's striae are a characteristic feature of:
questions.explanation: Wickham's striae are fine white lines on the surface of the violaceous, flat-topped, polygonal papules of lichen planus.

questions.text: The most common site of bleeding in anterior epistaxis in children and young adults is:
questions.explanation: Little's area on the anteroinferior nasal septum holds Kiesselbach's plexus, which is the source of most anterior nosebleeds. Woodruff's plexus is a site of posterior epistaxis in older adults.

questions.text: Classic phenylketonuria results from deficiency of which enzyme?
questions.explanation: Classic PKU is caused by phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency. Dihydropteridine reductase deficiency causes the less common malignant (BH4-deficient) variant.
